content:
alex: Heads-up — p99 in eu-west jumped after last rolling deploy, looks correlated with cross-region fallback hits. noticed this at ~08:12 UTC.

mari: saw that too, dashboards show a clear step change in p99 tokens for short requests (~16-64 tokens). p95 mostly stable.

kevin: can you paste the fallback logs? I want to see which region we fell back to and which kernel we picked.

alex: log snippet: ```
[08:12:23] route_decision: fallback -> us-east-1 (preferred eu capacity low)
[08:12:23] model_variant: redwood-7b-q4 (eu) -> redwood-7b-fp16 (us)
[08:12:23] kv_cache: miss (prefix key not found)
[08:12:24] token_emit_latency: 42ms (local kernel fp16)
[08:12:24] end_request: total_latency=220ms p99 spike
```
Looks like two things: fallback to a different quantization/kernel and cold KV cache on remote region.

sana: that aligns with profiling traces I pulled — when kernel mismatch happens we do an extra layout conversion memcpy + dequant step. adds ~10–18ms per token in the hot path.

luca: also, microbatch sizing matters here. our routing bursts push a bunch of tiny requests together; when we route them cross-region the remote host can't leverage the local prefix cache and we amplify KV miss rate. Microbatch=8 helped in eu, but when fallback hits to us-east the effective batch becomes smaller because we split by connection, so tail suffers.

kevin: TL;DR: two amplifiers for p99 — kernel-selection mismatch cost + KV cache miss amplification due to cross-region routing + microbatch fragmentation.

mari: propose quick mitigations: 1) pin model_variant compatibility during fallback (prefer quantized-compatible variants) 2) increase KV prefix TTL for eu->us fallback keys (short-term) 3) lower microbatch max for cross-region routed requests to reduce queuing jitter.

alex: experimented locally with a config tweak: `route_policy.allow_fallback_kernel_mismatch=false` and `kv.prefix_ttl_seconds=300` and p99 dropped ~60ms in our sim for synthetic 32-token workload. replicable script:```bash
# replay synthetic burst with X-Region header
for i in {1..200}; do
  curl -s -H "X-Region: eu-west" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --data '{"input":"hello world","max_tokens":32}' http://localhost:8080/v1/generate &
done
wait
```
results: p99 280ms -> 220ms after fixes.

kevin: nice. longer-term we should: - teach router to consider kernel compatibility score when selecting fallback region - emit kv_miss_rate per origin region in the trace - add microbatch-scaling policy that is route-aware (min_batch for cross-region).

sana: adding a note: the profiler shows that when fallback uses fp16 kernel instead of q4 with fused attention, we lose 1.8x token throughput on that worker. So fallback capacity planning needs model-variant parity or we accept the p99 hit.

luca: small experiment idea — try adaptive prefix caching: when we route requests from eu to us-east, replicate a tiny hotset of prefixes to us-east asynchronously (TTL 60s). could reduce kv misses without full replication. cheap and targeted.

mari: agree. I'll open a small-run RFC with two mutating experiments: (A) conservative fallback (kernel-aware) + kv-ttl bump, (B) async hotset replication + route-aware microbatch policy. run A on canary 10%, B on another 10%. metrics: p95/p99 tokens, kv_miss_rate, tokens/sec, cost delta.

alex: tagging deploy-bot to coordinate canary windows. :eyes:

deploy-bot: Scheduled canary rollout for eng-runtime/canary at 2026-04-02T09:00:00Z, groups: 10% A, 10% B. Notifying infra.

kevin: one more ask — when you capture traces for the canary, include kernel name and `kernel_mismatch=true/false` as span attributes so we can aggregate p99 by mismatch bucket.

sana: will do. i'll also capture per-token memcpy time slices.

mari: great thread. i'll write the RFC tonight and link here. thanks everyone. :rocket:
